name: Design Fictions
description:
Design fiction explores possible worlds through fictional but tangible representations of products, services, systems or media. These artefacts are often presented as though they belong to another present or a possible future.

By making an imagined condition concrete enough to encounter and discuss, design fiction can help people examine how technologies might intersect with everyday life, institutions, behaviours and values.
whenToUse:
Use design fiction when abstract discussion of future possibilities is insufficient and a project would benefit from making assumptions or consequences tangible.

It is useful for emerging technologies, strategic exploration, futures work and critical discussion.
steps: Identify the change or question to explore.
Research relevant technological and social conditions.
Develop a coherent fictional world or premise.
Decide what everyday artefact could provide a glimpse into that world.
Create the artefact with enough detail to suggest its surrounding context.
Consider secondary consequences: who uses it, who provides it and what institutions support it?
Present the fiction to an audience.
Use reactions and discussion to examine assumptions, consequences and alternative possibilities.
lookOutFor: A futuristic-looking object is not automatically design fiction; the surrounding world matters.
Avoid presenting speculative propositions as forecasts.
Consider whose future is represented and whose experience is absent.

resources.citation: Bleecker, J. (2009). *Design Fiction: A Short Essay on Design, Science, Fact and Fiction*.
Dunne, A. & Raby, F. (2013). *Speculative Everything*. MIT Press.
